facts.raw_span: a woman in her 60s presented with an itchy plaque on the mid-back
had had a lesion at that site since childhood, which had remained asymptomatic and pea sized for most of that time
over the 10 years prior to presentation it had gradually increased in size and became itchy
occasional oozing of serosanguineous fluid and bleeding from the lesion
1.5 × 1.0-cm well-defined erythematous plaque with overlying ulceration on the mid-back, 1 cm left of the spine
adjoining skin showed a horseshoe-shaped oval area of lichenification
circumscribed tumor contiguous with adjoining normal epidermis and delineated from underlying dermis by continuous apocrine epithelial lining
tumor epithelium with multiple papillary projections with vascular, plasma cell–rich stroma
several foci showed papillary projections lined by multilayered epithelium with atypical cells, few mitotic figures, and areas of necrosis but no dermal invasion
p63 staining positive in myoepithelial cell layers
adjacent skin showed dermal papillae with congophilic amorphous eosinophilic deposits
pan-cytokeratin (AE1/3) immunostain positive

concepts.why: The presence of a circumscribed tumor with papillary projections and a vascular, plasma cell-rich stroma, along with positive p63 staining in myoepithelial cell layers, supports the diagnosis of Hidradenoma Papilliferum.

The combination of a well-defined erythematous plaque with overlying ulceration, along with histopathological findings of a tumor with papillary projections and a vascular, plasma cell-rich stroma, suggests Syringocystadenoma Papilliferum.
The presence of a tumor with papillary projections and a vascular, plasma cell-rich stroma, along with positive p63 staining in myoepithelial cell layers, supports the diagnosis of Eccrine Poroma.

The combination of a well-defined erythematous plaque with overlying ulceration, along with histopathological findings of a tumor with papillary projections and a vascular, plasma cell-rich stroma, suggests Apocrine Hidradenoma.
The presence of a horseshoe-shaped oval area of lichenification, along with dermal papillae with congophilic amorphous eosinophilic deposits, supports the diagnosis of Lichen Simplex Chronicus.
The combination of a long-standing itchy plaque with occasional oozing of serosanguineous fluid and bleeding, along with a horseshoe-shaped oval area of lichenification, suggests Prurigo Nodularis.
The presence of a well-defined erythematous plaque with overlying ulceration, along with a horseshoe-shaped oval area of lichenification, supports the diagnosis of Seborrheic Keratosis.
The combination of a well-defined erythematous plaque with overlying ulceration, along with a horseshoe-shaped oval area of lichenification, suggests Dermatofibroma.

rationales.F01: Itchy plaque presentation is common in several skin conditions.
rationales.F03: Gradual increase in size and itchiness over 10 years suggests a possible neoplastic process.
rationales.F05: Well-defined erythematous plaque with ulceration is a distinctive clinical feature.
rationales.F06: Lichenification is a common feature of chronic skin conditions.
rationales.F07: Circumscribed tumor with apocrine epithelial lining is characteristic of certain adnexal tumors.
rationales.F08: Papillary projections with vascular stroma are typical of certain adnexal tumors.
rationales.F09: Atypical cells and mitotic figures suggest a possible malignant process.
rationales.F10: p63 staining positive in myoepithelial cell layers supports the diagnosis of certain adnexal tumors.
rationales.F12: Pan-cytokeratin positivity is a common feature of epithelial tumors.
